Strait of Hormuz Status: October 15, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  228 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
15 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.76 -1.13 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 A container ship has sunk in the Strait of Hormuz, per gCaptain, which captured containers and debris floating in the waterway.

02 The Washington Post reports Iranian attacks have sunk two ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

03 Brent stood at $104.76, down 1.13% over 24 hours, as of 12:12 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Washington Post reports Iranian attacks have sunk two ships in the strait. The GFS Pride, a Singapore-flagged container vessel reported on October 14, remains in the news: maritime security sources cited by Reuters say it sank after a projectile strike, and the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said two Singapore-registered vessels were struck by unknown projectiles, one sinking after catching fire and the other sustaining hull damage, per MarineLink. Reuters also reports that two commercial ships were sunk by projectile attacks near the strait. A cargo ship sank after striking a mine in the strait, the IRGC claims, a claim no major wire in this feed carries independently. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $104.76, down 1.13% over 24 hours, as of 12:12 UTC. The freight derivatives market is adapting: Hellenic Shipping News reports that ICE's newly launched TD34 Forward Freight Agreement, covering the Gulf of Oman to China route, has seen near-record trading volumes since its October 5 debut, outpacing the established TD3C contract as market participants seek greater Gulf freight cover. The feed indexed 113 headlines across the crisis in the last 24 hours. As of 12:22 UTC, 130 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
